brief.input: Synthetic case: recycled HDPE and nylon offcuts; their proportions are unknown.
brief.variation: The proportions and visible grit change between received portions.
brief.contamination: Grit identity and amount are not measured.
brief.use_case: A proposed walking surface in a wet doorway; no prototype has been made.
brief.targets: Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.
brief.process: A press is available; its type and tooling have not been confirmed.
brief.available_changes: No new materials, equipment or geometry changes are authorized yet.

plan.answer: You can work with this variable HDPE/nylon + grit mix without new materials or geometry yet by keeping portions separate, preparing by inspection only, and testing the same shape in a controlled way. Any binder, drainage-hole change, or new tooling needs explicit permission because your case currently authorizes no new materials, equipment or geometry changes, and press type/tooling is unconfirmed.

material_routes.title: Keep portions separate, test range
material_routes.change: Preparation only, no new binder or equipment: keep each received portion separate and do not blend across portions.
material_routes.why: Proportions and visible grit change between portions, so mixing hides the cause. Separate trials use the variation as information without needing composition measurement.
steps: Label each incoming portion with date and visual notes on colour, stiffness, and visible grit.
Keep offcuts from different portions in separate containers.
Make trial pieces portion-by-portion using only currently authorized means.
Record which portion gave better water clearing and wet grip.
tradeoffs: Shows range but does not remove variation.
May produce different results per portion.
material_routes.check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by comparing trials from different portions made the same way.

material_routes.title: Inspect and separate loose grit
material_routes.change: Preparation only, no new materials: visual sort plus removal of loose surface grit, conditional on safe manual handling and suitable facilities.
material_routes.why: Grit identity and amount are not measured, and grit can affect drainage and slip. Removing only the loose fraction lowers one unknown without adding a binder.
steps: Visually separate obvious HDPE pieces, nylon offcuts, and heavily gritted pieces where possible.
Shake/brush off only loose surface grit; do not grind or create dust.
Set heavily gritted material aside as its own portion.
Keep notes on how much was separated per portion.
tradeoffs: Does not identify grit chemistry or amount.
Manual sorting is slow and subjective.
Washing, drying or grinding would need unconfirmed capability.
material_routes.check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by observing drainage blocking and wet-surface feel before and after preparation for the same portion.

engineering_routes.title: Same-shape controlled trial log
engineering_routes.change: No geometry change: use only the already-intended insert shape and log press conditions the same way each run. This route does not assume heated, cold, mould, drying or extraction capability - press type and tooling remain unconfirmed.
engineering_routes.why: When proportions and grit vary, a consistent process and placement reduces reliance on unknown material properties and shows whether results follow the portion.
steps: Confirm what your press can safely do with HDPE/nylon offcuts with grit before making product trials.
Make one trial per incoming portion without mixing portions.
Keep placement, slope/support, and water application the same and change one variable at a time.
Record portion ID, preparation, press observation, and drainage/slip observation together.
tradeoffs: Does not fix variation, only reveals it.
Needs careful labelling and repeat placement.
Press use stays on hold until capability is confirmed.
engineering_routes.check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by placing each portion-linked trial the same way and observing water clearing and wet-foot grip side-by-side.

engineering_routes.title: Conditional lift-out contained insert - needs permission
engineering_routes.change: CONFLICT: this would change geometry/containment and needs new capability, which your case says is not authorized yet. Use as a conditional option only if geometry and containment work are permitted.
engineering_routes.why: Containment and a cleanable path separate walking safety from unknown grit and blend variation, but it cannot start without geometry and tooling permission.
steps: Ask whether a contained, lift-out insert with cleanable drainage path is permitted.
If permitted, keep the outer footprint fixed and treat internal openings and containment as adjustable design choices.
Compare cleaning and water-clearing between portions using the same test placement.
Retain the preparation decision from Material Lab with or without this architecture.
tradeoffs: Not allowed under current no-geometry-change limit.
May need unconfirmed moulds, forming tools or extraction.
Adds joints/edges that need slip and trip observation.
engineering_routes.check: Check against 'Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance; numerical acceptance limits are not set.' by observing whether water leaves the walking surface and whether grit can be cleaned out without dismantling the doorway.

next_steps: Confirm what is permitted: manual sorting, use of the existing press, and any geometry or tooling change.
Confirm press type, tooling, and safe processing information for HDPE/nylon with grit before any heated trial.
Make portion-linked trials the same way and compare water clearing and wet-slip observation.
Decide a simple pass observation for drainage and wet grip since numerical acceptance limits are not set.
questions: Is any preparation beyond manual inspection/sorting permitted, and is heated pressing of this grit-containing HDPE/nylon mix permitted with your current facilities?
Would you allow a geometry change such as drainage openings or a lift-out contained insert if testing shows it helps?
How will you judge Drain surface water and maintain wet-slip resistance in practice - water volume, slope, footwear, and cleaning frequency?

sources.title: Basel Convention — plastic waste preparation and recycling
sources.scope: General guidance on identifying, preparing and sorting plastic streams and material-specific compatibility. It supplies no binder identity, additive dose or performance prediction for the user's mix.

sources.title: Cecon 2021 — measured recycled-PE blends
sources.scope: The study's PE blends and injection process only. It illustrates measuring a response at separate recycled-content levels, not a density or recipe for another material.

sources.title: HSE — controlling fume during plastics processing
sources.scope: General guidance to identify polymer formulation/additives and processing information before heated processing. Temperature and dwell affect fumes; this is not a heat recipe for unidentified cable residue.
